36 The diagram shows a circuit.
V
Which statement about the circuit is not correct?
A
Electromotive force is the energy transferred per unit charge.
B
Energy is transferred from chemical potential energy in the cell to other forms when the
switch is closed.
C
The electromotive force of the cell is greater than the terminal potential difference when the
switch is closed.
D
When the switch is open, the voltmeter measures the electromotive force of the cell.

hints: Look at where the voltmeter is connected - it is directly across the lamp, not directly across the cell terminals.
Recall that e.m.f. is measured across the cell when no current flows, which needs the voltmeter to form a complete loop with the cell terminals.
Check what happens when the left-hand switch is open - trace a path from the cell through the voltmeter and see if the circuit is broken.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: the dashed box contains the cell plus its internal resistance, in series with the switch and the lamp, and the voltmeter $V$ is in parallel with the lamp only.
Recall the rules: e.m.f. $E$ is energy transferred per unit charge by the cell, and terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir$ when current $I$ flows through internal resistance $r$.

Test statements A, B and C: A states the definition of e.m.f., B describes chemical to electrical to light and heat conversion when current flows, and C states $E > V$ when closed due to lost volts $Ir$ - all are correct.

Test statement D: to read e.m.f. the voltmeter must be connected across the cell with $I = 0$. Here with the switch open, the left wire to the voltmeter is disconnected from the cell, so no complete connection to both cell terminals exists.
Therefore the voltmeter reads $0$, not $E$, when the switch is open, making D the statement that is not correct. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is correct physics, so it cannot be the not-correct statement. Electromotive force $E$ is defined as work done per unit charge $E = W/Q$.

B.explanation: This is correct physics. Closing the switch allows current, so chemical energy in the cell is converted to electrical energy and then to light and heat in the lamp and internal resistance.

C.explanation: This is correct physics. When closed, $V = E - Ir$, so some e.m.f. is lost across internal resistance and terminal p.d. $V$ is less than $E$.

D.explanation: This is not correct. With the switch open the voltmeter is across the lamp only and is disconnected from the cell on the left, so it reads zero, not the e.m.f.
